name: Flexibility of Closure
definition: The ability to identify or detect a known pattern (a figure, object, word, or sound) that is hidden in other distracting material.

benchmark.name: COD10K
benchmark.metric: Structure-measure S-alpha on the COD10K test set (2,026 images), scale 0-1, higher is better
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population doing careful visual search and outlining on still images, since Flexibility of Closure is a general perceptual ability used across many jobs

benchmark.name: COD10K
benchmark.metric: weighted F-measure (F^w_β) on COD10K-Test, 0.686 written as a percentage
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce performing visual search for a hidden or camouflaged target. Flexibility of closure is a broad perceptual ability, not a specialist skill. The assumed setting is a typical adult with reasonable viewing time who is told a concealed object is present, marking its extent.

benchmark.name: COD10K
benchmark.metric: S-measure (Sα, structure similarity from 0 to 1; higher is better)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce with normal vision. Flexibility of Closure is a broad perceptual ability used in inspection, search, and surveillance-type work, not a specialist skill.

benchmark.name: COD10K
benchmark.metric: S-measure (structure measure, 0-1 scale, higher is better) on the COD10K test set (2,026 images)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce doing careful visual search or inspection (for example image annotators, visual inspectors), working without time pressure

benchmark.name: COD10K
benchmark.metric: S-measure (structure similarity, 0-1 scale; higher is better)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce performing careful visual search and localization, such as inspection, surveillance or image-review workers, with adequate viewing time and knowledge that a concealed object is present

benchmark.name: VisFactor
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on the Closure Flexibility subtests CF1-CF3
